draft.title: Area of any triangle
card: \(\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}ab \sin C\). Here \(a\) and \(b\) are two sides, and \(C\) is the angle between them.
It works for any triangle, because \(a \sin C\) acts as the height. You do not need to measure the height.
Example: sides 8 cm and 5 cm with 30° between them. \(\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 5 \times \sin 30^{\circ} = 20 \times 0.5 = 10 \text{ cm}^{2}\).
To find an angle from a known area, rearrange to \(\sin C = \frac{2 \times \text{Area}}{ab}\) and take the inverse sine.
draft.remember: Half the product of two sides, times the sine of the angle between them.

a.q: A triangular garden bed has two edges of 9 m and 12 m that meet at an angle of 40°. What is its area, to 1 decimal place?
a.why: \(\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 12 \times \sin 40^{\circ}\), which is \(54 \times 0.6428 = 34.7 \text{ m}^{2}\). Using \(\cos 40^{\circ}\) gives \(41.4 \text{ m}^{2}\), which uses the wrong ratio.
a.clue: Half, times both sides, times the sine.

b.q: A triangle has an area of \(20 \text{ cm}^{2}\). Two sides measure 8 cm and 10 cm, and the angle \(C\) between them is acute. What is \(C\)?
b.why: \(20 = \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 10 \times \sin C = 40 \sin C\), so \(\sin C = 0.5\) and \(C = 30^{\circ}\). Forgetting the \(\frac{1}{2}\) gives \(\sin C = 0.25\), which is 14.5°.
b.clue: Write the area formula, then solve for \(\sin C\).
